canonical.title: Living in both OSes: running Windows and Linux for months without your setup rotting

parent.title: Testing the waters: a staged, reversible path from a Windows dev workstation to Linux

siblings.title: The staged ladder: what each rung of a Windows→Linux move actually proves
siblings.summary: A rung-by-rung ladder from WSL2 to full switch, with what each rung proves, what it structurally hides, the go/no-go signal, and the cost of retreating.

siblings.title: WSL2 as rung zero — what it proves, and the exact wall it hits
siblings.summary: WSL2 retires every userland risk in a Linux migration and none of the machine-ownership risks; here is where the line falls in 2026.

siblings.title: Dual-boot Linux next to Windows in 2026 without wrecking the Windows install
siblings.summary: Buy a second NVMe, keep the two OSes ignorant of each other, and pick Linux from the firmware boot menu — the layout with the smallest blast radius on your Windows install.

siblings.title: Dropbox on Linux and shared folders: what actually works in 2026
siblings.summary: The official Linux client now supports btrfs/zfs/xfs, but you cannot share one Dropbox folder between a Windows and a Linux install, and code repos do not belong in Dropbox at all.

siblings.title: Trial hardware and VM paths for evaluating Linux before you commit (2026)
siblings.summary: Live USB first (€10, 15 minutes, proves your actual hardware), then a full install on an external NVMe SSD (€90–150) — everything else is a detour.

siblings.title: Exit criteria and the blocker inventory: decide the Linux switch on evidence, not vibes
siblings.summary: A fill-in blocker inventory plus tickable go/no-go criteria and a pre-committed rollback date for a Windows-to-Linux workstation trial.

sources.title: chezmoi — dotfile manager comparison table
sources.claim: Feature matrix of dotfile managers: chezmoi, dotbot, rcm, vcsh, yadm and bare git compared on Windows support, private files, whole-file encryption, password-manager integration, diffs, templating and run-once scripts.

sources.title: chezmoi — Windows user guide
sources.claim: chezmoi branches per-OS via .chezmoi.os and detects WSL through .chezmoi.kernel.osrelease; on Windows symlink creation needs developer mode or SeCreateSymbolicLinkPrivilege and elevated scripts need Start-Process -Wait.

sources.title: chezmoi — password managers
sources.claim: chezmoi pulls secrets at apply time from 1Password, Bitwarden (bw, bws, rbw) and pass, or encrypts committed files with age/gpg, so secrets never live in the dotfiles repo.

sources.title: GNU Stow
sources.claim: GNU Stow is a Perl symlink-farm manager and depends on the filesystem supporting symbolic links, with no documented Windows support.

sources.title: NixOS Discourse — home-manager inside NixOS-WSL
sources.claim: home-manager reaches Windows only through WSL, and symlinks it creates in a Windows directory cannot be read by Windows programs including git and git bash.

sources.title: home-manager (nix-community)
sources.claim: home-manager is the Nix-based declarative user-environment manager; it has no native Windows target.

sources.title: Hacker News — dotfile manager discussion
sources.claim: Hacker News commenters who evaluated Stow and trialled chezmoi report settling on yadm for lower ceremony.

sources.title: BigGo — dotfile management tools comparison
sources.claim: Community pain point with yadm is identical content that must live at different paths on different operating systems; yadm covers OS variation only via ##os.Linux / ##os.Darwin alternate files.

sources.title: git-config documentation
sources.claim: Definitions for conditional includes (includeIf gitdir/gitdir-i/onbranch/hasconfig) and for core.fileMode, core.symlinks, core.ignoreCase and core.autocrlf.

sources.title: Fun with Linux — sharing a git repo on an NTFS partition
sources.claim: Sharing a git working tree on an NTFS partition between Linux and Windows requires uid/gid/dmask/fmask mount options plus core.filemode false and core.ignorecase true, and still produces phantom modifications and ownership conflicts.

sources.title: Subzerodays — creating a git repo on NTFS in Linux
sources.claim: git init on an NTFS mount can fail outright because chmod is not permitted on the filesystem.

sources.title: LKML — “ntfs filesystem remake” patch series (Jan 2026)
sources.claim: In January 2026 Namjae Jeon posted an 'ntfs filesystem remake' patch series to LKML arguing ntfs3 is poorly maintained, with the replacement passing 308 xfstests versus ntfs3's 235.

sources.title: Dedoimedo — Linux NTFS driver reliability
sources.claim: Field reports of the in-kernel ntfs3 driver include out-of-memory on large copies, hangs and data loss; blacklisting ntfs3 in favour of the slower ntfs-3g restores reliability.

sources.title: Pope Kim — Stop using core.autocrlf
sources.claim: 2025 guidance is to stop relying on per-machine core.autocrlf and commit a .gitattributes instead, since only the repo-level file is enforced across machines.

sources.title: Microsoft Learn — Git case sensitivity
sources.claim: Git is case-sensitive but Windows and macOS filesystems are not, so checking out File.txt and file.txt on Windows leaves only one file and folders differing only by case get merged.

sources.title: Microsoft Tech Community — OneDrive is corrupting my Git repositories
sources.claim: Cloud file-sync clients corrupt git repositories placed inside synced folders; the recommendation is to keep repos outside the sync root.

sources.title: SQLPey — Git and Dropbox safe practices
sources.claim: Dropbox's file-sync model lacks the atomicity guarantees git relies on; git-remote-dropbox goes through the Dropbox API rather than the desktop client's file operations and is the safe way to use Dropbox as a remote.

sources.title: Git Credential Manager — credential stores
sources.claim: Git Credential Manager uses different credential store backends per OS: wincredman/dpapi on Windows, secretservice (requires a GUI session) or gpg/pass on Linux.

sources.title: Baeldung — libsecret as the Linux git credential provider
sources.claim: git-credential-libsecret is the current Linux credential helper; the older libgnome-keyring helper has been deprecated since January 2014.

sources.title: PowerShell — Unix support and platform differences
sources.claim: PowerShell on Linux stores its profile at ~/.config/powershell/profile.ps1 and lacks COM, Get-WinEvent, Get-CimInstance and the ActiveDirectory module; paths are case-sensitive and .NET Framework modules do not load.

sources.title: Redmond Magazine — a smarter cross-platform PowerShell profile
sources.claim: A single PowerShell profile can be written to branch on platform so one file serves both Windows and Linux.

sources.title: Yubico — Securing SSH with FIDO2
sources.claim: An ed25519-sk resident key (ssh-keygen -O resident, firmware 5.2.3+ with a FIDO2 PIN) stores the credential on the token so the same key works on Windows and Linux without copying a private key.

sources.title: Brandon Checketts — SSH ed25519 key best practices for 2025
sources.claim: 2025 best practice is one SSH key per client machine so a leak is attributable and blast radius is limited, rather than copying one private key everywhere.

sources.title: 1Password — SSH agent
sources.claim: The 1Password SSH agent serves keys from the vault to git and ssh clients on Windows, macOS and Linux without the client ever reading the private key; an agent config file selects which keys a given machine uses.

sources.title: tobywf — Ditch GnuPG, sign commits with SSH
sources.claim: Git has supported SSH commit signing since 2.34 via gpg.format=ssh, configured with user.signingkey, commit.gpgsign and gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile, removing the need for GPG agents on both OSes.

sources.title: Yubico — Securing git with SSH and FIDO2
sources.claim: A FIDO2 -sk SSH key can be used to sign git commits, keeping authentication and signing on the same hardware token.

sources.title: VS Code — Settings Sync
sources.claim: VS Code Settings Sync covers settings, keybindings, snippets, tasks, UI state, extensions and profiles; keybindings sync per platform by default and machine-scoped settings are excluded.

sources.title: JetBrains Rider — Sharing your IDE settings
sources.claim: Rider's Backup and Sync plugin is bundled and enabled by default and syncs themes, keymaps, colour schemes, editor and code-style settings, live templates and the enabled-plugin list under a JetBrains Account.

sources.title: It's FOSS News — Microsoft retires the Teams Linux app
sources.claim: Microsoft retired the native Teams desktop client for Linux and replaced it with a progressive web app.

sources.title: How-To Geek — Firefox Sync that actually works
sources.claim: Firefox Sync is end-to-end encrypted and syncs extension settings and data, which Chrome does not; Chrome and Firefox sync payloads are cryptographically incompatible.

sources.title: Microsoft Learn — Safe storage of app secrets (user-secrets)
sources.claim: dotnet user-secrets writes to %APPDATA%\Microsoft\UserSecrets\<id>\secrets.json on Windows and ~/.microsoft/usersecrets/<id>/secrets.json on Linux/macOS — per-user, per-OS, outside the project.

sources.title: Microsoft Learn — NuGet global packages and cache folders
sources.claim: The NuGet global packages folder defaults to %userprofile%\.nuget\packages on Windows and ~/.nuget/packages on Linux/macOS, overridable via NUGET_PACKAGES.

sources.title: Microsoft Learn — global.json overview
sources.claim: global.json pins which .NET SDK the CLI uses, requires a full version number, offers rollForward policies such as latestFeature, and since .NET 10 supports a paths array (e.g. [".dotnet", "$host$"]) plus a custom errorMessage for repo-local SDKs.

sources.title: containers.dev — Development Containers specification
sources.claim: The Development Containers specification is an open standard where devcontainer.json describes the whole development environment — OS, runtime, tools, settings — as code, supported by a range of tools rather than one vendor.

sources.title: .NET Blog — Exploring new .NET releases with Dev Containers
sources.claim: Microsoft documents dev containers as the way to try new .NET SDK releases without altering the host machine's installation.

sources.title: How-To Geek — WSL2 projects on the Windows filesystem are slower
sources.claim: Under WSL2, files accessed through /mnt/c cross a Linux/Windows boundary and run roughly 2x to 10x slower; git is disproportionately affected because it stats many files.

sources.title: microsoft/WSL issue #4197 — /mnt filesystem performance
sources.claim: Long-running upstream issue tracking WSL2 filesystem performance in /mnt being much slower than WSL1.
